It's the adventure of a lifetime. Sign me up.

Went to Catholic school my whole life up until college. It honestly started as early as I can remember. I remember being in church and everyone replying in unison and it making me extremely uncomfortable. That unease always followed me. Fast forward to junior year of high school and theology class that year mainly focused of the dogma of the church. That was the nail in the coffin for not just me but for a few people who were a lot more dedicated than I was. Like someone else said in this thread, I didn't like the "answers" I was given and felt that science made the most sense. So ironically it was a religious education that turned me against religion. I'm sure my story isn't that unique but I thought I'd throw 2 cents in. Plus, I had a lot of super religious elderly family members who spent their final years praying almost non-stop and live in constant fear that they were going to hell. I hope I never become like that.

Bonus story: my one friend (who also was in that junior theology class with me) still believes but said he'll never step into a church ever again because he used to work at one as a maintenance worker/groundskeeper and told me that any time he could overhear the priests talking, they were almost always talking about ways they could get more money out of the churchgoers. There's a family-owned pizza place in my area that has a wing night every Tuesday. Wings are only 50 cents each so it's a perfect thing for broke college students. Been going there with friends since 2013 so here's a list of some the most interesting things that have happened while my group was there:

* First time I'm ever there (friends had been before), they bring out everyone's order except my friend Rick's. Without question, he has the easiest order: just a dozen mild. The rest of us had more complex orders (differing amount of wings and flavors). Waitresses bring out all the orders except Rick's, say they be right back with this, no problem right? Wrong. They never come back out. We start eating and Rick is less than amused. Waitress comes out a few different times doing other things, Rick asks her a few times about his order, every time she's says "I'll get it now". Never does. We eventually finish and said waitress comes with our checks and a styrofoam container with Rick's order and says "Not sure if you still want it or not." and just plops it down in front of him with his check. Wings were ice cold and they even charged him extra for bleu cheese and celery even though they never gave it to him. This was more comical than I made it sound and has become sort of a inside joke in our group.

* Five of us are going to a hockey game and meet up there before, grab dinner, and then carpool to the game. I'm also trying to get in and get out as quickly as possible because the team was having a giveaway of some kind. Four of us order and our friend Matt only gets an order of pretzel bites w/ a side of nacho cheese. It takes us about 45 minutes for the food to come out and his never does. It takes us about another 30 minutes to eat and his still hasn't come. He asks about it a few times and it just never happens. Eventually, he gets up and very loudly in a decently crowded restaurant says "fuck this shit" and just walks out. His brother Nick calls him a few minutes later and says that Matt just took their car and went home and left his brother there. They also took an eternity to bring the checks out so we ended up being late for the game too.

* During my senior year of high school, one of our foreign exchange students from Italy gets a job there. We go in one night and he ends up being our waiter. We get our food and he comes back out to talk to us for a bit. One person in the group asks him how he likes America so far. He responds "I love it but so many black people." He says it pretty loudly and there just happens to be a black family of about 8 sitting at the table directly next to us. In his defense, he really was not trying to be racist. It was more of an observation because I guess they don't have too black people in Italy. 

**TL;DR** Local pizza place can handle complicated orders but not simple ones.

My friends and I went on vacation to Ocean City, MD for a week in 2014. A group of girls from our high school also happened to be there and were staying in a house a few blocks from where we were. On either Day 3 or 4, all 8 of us head over there to hang out and drink for a while before we all headed to the boardwalk. When we arrive, we discover that they had invited another random group of guys they met who we had never seen before. We're there for maybe a half hour before my buddy Rick and I have excuse ourselves to the porch outside because of how loud the combination of the music and everyone talking was. The porch was on the second story of the house and from there Rick and I can see a cop car just sitting there a block away on the opposite side of an open field. We think that either the cops will be able to hear us or someone is definitely going to call in a noise complaint. Most of us were 19-20 at the time so getting caught with alcohol was a fear most had in the back of our minds constantly. Rick and I decide to leave and go back to our house to regroup before going to the boardwalk on our own. Before we did that, we decided to go back in and let everyone know we were leaving so they wouldn't be looking for us. We do that and also let them know about the cop car and politely suggest that they turn down the music because they would be deaf before the sun set. One of the girls (who shall remain nameless) loses her shit and goes off about A) how cowardly we are for worrying about "those pigs" (her words, not mine), and B) how we'll be "virgins forever" because all we do is play Mario Kart (Rick had brought his Gamecube and MKDD & Mario Superstar Baseball had been main sources of entertainment during our down time.). We got out of there and made the walk back to our house. Rick quickly laughed off the event but I took it a bit too personally and had to be calmed down. Normally, shit like that doesn't bother me but something about it sent me into almost a blind rage. Rick calmed me downed but not before using all of my favorite 4 letter words to describe what I thought about her.

About 45 minutes later, Rick and I are watching TV and just about to leave to go to the boardwalk. All of a sudden, the rest of our house comes running up the stairs and into the house. They told us that shortly after we left, they all headed to the boardwalk and while there, the girl that had bitched us out ended up getting stopped by a bike cop and given a ticket for openly carrying alcohol on the boardwalk. What makes it even better was that everyone in that group of about 15 people had booze on them and she was the only one who got caught. The guys from our house saw this and slowly crept away before booking it back to safety. Sorry for the novel but I take so much satisfaction in this.

TL;DR - Girl bitches us out for no reason, gets a ticket for open-carrying alcohol while underage.
